artifacts.summary: 4-phase plan (4.5h) landing the (c) ruling -- a declaration-only obligation in checkpoint-commit.md with a pointer from general-implementation-agent.md, a Site-2 derived-output-prefix splice so a regenerated declared surface is actually stageable, a non-blocking derived_probe_run_all backstop at the phase-commit site, and a deploy/verify close.

memory_candidates.content: The derived-output-prefix widening (derived_probe_output_prefixes from scripts/lib/derived-artifact-probe-lib.sh) is spliced at Containment Site 1 (orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh WORK h) and Site 3 (git-commit-scoped.sh's V10), but NOT at Site 2 (git-commit-phase.sh's Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check). git-staging-scope.md's own 'Three Containment sites, not one' section already records why Site 3 cannot compensate: Site 2 removes an uncontained path from its own files_touched array, and therefore from the pathspec, before git-commit-scoped.sh is ever invoked, and V10 tests only the pathspec entries it is handed. The same asymmetry is already documented there for the own-task-directory member. Consequence: a declared derived-output path regenerated mid-phase is dropped at Site 2 with a 'scope excursion' row unless it is independently inside the task's declared file_scope -- so any prose obligation to re-run a generator and stage its output within the phase is undone at the commit unless Site 2 gains the same splice.
